references.text: God is referred to as 'the Rock' with perfect ways, using the same imagery and theme of God's perfection
The Lord is called 'my Rock,' and it is affirmed that there is no injustice in him, reflecting the same theme of God's righteousness
The Lord is described as an eternal rock, using the same imagery of God as the Rock
The Lord is righteous in all his ways, parallel to the statement that all his ways are right
Moses' song is mentioned, and God's ways are described as just and true, a direct allusion to this text
God is faithful and righteous, highlighting the theme of God's faithfulness and righteousness
The Lord's word is right, and all his work is faithful, parallel to the idea that his work is perfect
All God's works are truth, and his ways are right, a direct parallel to the theme of God's perfect ways
The same context appears in Moses' song where God is referred to as the Rock
God is called the Rock in Hannah's song of praise, using the same imagery
